key_findings: Claim-driven allocation preserves the manipulability found in #7146: across all three non-truth reporting policies, 22.2222% of comparable focal outcomes improve relative to the paired truthful counterpart, with mean gain 1.3274074 ticks and maximum gain 14.
Verified-truth authority eliminates the measured focal reporting advantage: 4,050 comparable non-truth paired completions have zero positive gain.

Mismatch-rejected authority also eliminates positive gain, but by refusing mismatched focal declarations: 100% of criticality-inflation and dual-misreport cells are rejected; liquidity-demand underreporting is rejected in 54.1667% of cells.
Mismatch rejection therefore trades manipulation resistance for lower focal/system completion in the synthetic model; it is not interchangeable with verified truth.
authority_boundary_result:: The model distinguishes assertion, verification, and rejection as separate authority semantics rather than treating a declaration as truth.
design_implication: A durable allocation design should bind each allocation input to an explicit authority/provenance mode. 'Declared by participant' and 'verified fact' must not be semantically interchangeable.
claim_ceiling: Synthetic deterministic authority/manipulability observation only; no empirical truthfulness, equilibrium, incentive-compatibility, welfare, or real-system safety claim.
